top_strength: The probe was excellent — effectively a clean sweep. Joel confirmed the apartment number, square footage, and both addresses against the file, then worked through additional areas, elevator-to-truck distance, elevator-to-door walk, heavy items, glass/marble/stone, appliances, work equipment, antiques, book collections, box count, and who was packing. Two moments stand out. He caught that the destination had changed from a first-floor to a second-floor unit and immediately asked 'are we going to have easy access to the stairwell?' And he then used what he learned to correct the estimate rather than rubber-stamping the auto-booking: 'I went ahead and up the estimate by an hour and fifteen minutes... the walking distance there at that first location is gonna add a little bit of time.' That is exactly the estimate-accuracy behavior we want — the clock block was also textbook, covering on-site start, contract signing, the 2.5 hour minimum, and 15-minute increments in one clean pass.
coaching_note: Joel, this call was strong where it counts most on accuracy — you re-verified an auto-booked quote, caught the floor change and the long walk, and adjusted the estimate up instead of letting the system's number ride. Keep doing that. The highest-leverage fix is the delivery of the money moment: your pricing, clock, and estimate all came out as one continuous paragraph, and Dylan's only replies were 'Oh.' and 'Oh.' He did not absorb it. Break it into three beats and stop for a real answer after each — 'So pricing is super simple: it's a flat hourly rate for a two-mover crew and everything's included... does that make sense so far?' Then the clock. Then the number. And when you ask 'any questions there?' and get a non-answer, ask again: 'just want to make sure that number landed right — what are you thinking?' Second priority: you gave the rate and the no-hidden-fees pitch but skipped all three trust differentiators. Add 'you're covered by our No Worries damage coverage, up to $2,000 to repair, replace, or reimburse anything we damage,' plus Meet Your Mover and the On-Time Guarantee, and mention there's no deposit — that last one costs you five seconds and it's why people pick us. Third: a 650 sqft self-pack with a 200-foot walk to the elevator is the best Save Your Ass case there is, because every box he carries out himself is a trip your movers don't make down that hallway. And say his name — you asked for it and then never used it once.
phone_presence_notes: Polite, efficient, and patient through the customer's date flip-flopping, but transactional throughout — no name use, a clear rapport opening (the couch joke) left on the table, and the pricing block delivered as a monologue the customer plainly did not follow.
audio_review_reason: The quote delivery is transcribed with mangled figures ('$9,085 and a half hours', 'save your mover to take about $4') against a stated $204/hour rate, and the customer's responses through that entire stretch are only 'Oh.' — audio is needed to tell whether Joel actually misspoke the price or the transcript garbled it, and whether the customer ever confirmed comprehension.
